messages.author: b756a7daa2c2aa6d
messages.subject: Re: split plot and vertical shaded background
parts:
> Once I have this plot, above it, I'd like to do exactly the same but
> with the three theta variables. Is there an easy way to connect these
> two plots? The data is too dense (block extends into the tens of
> millions) to want to have two y axes on the same figure, so it is
> important to have two separate plots.
>
> Finally, I'd like to have vertical shading in the background that
> darkens any region that has "yes" in the second column (Inversion).

Here's a couple of ideas:

r <- read.table(textConnection("block Inversion mcov mtheta

0.003858893"),header=T)
closeAllConnections()


library(ggplot2)
ggplot(r, aes(block), colour = 1) +
geom_point(aes(y = mcov, colour = "m")) +
geom_point(aes(y = scov, colour = "s")) +
geom_point(aes(y = pestcov, colour = "pest")) +
labs(y = "cov", colour = "type")

# Alternatively you could switch to the molten form of the data

# Make it easier to split up the components
names(r) <- c("block", "Inversion", "m.cov", "m.theta", "s.cov",
"s.theta", "pest.cov", "pest.theta")

rm <- melt(r, id = 1:2)
rm <- cbind(rm, colsplit(rm$variable, "\\.", c("var", "type")))

qplot(block, value, data = subset(rm, type == "cov"), colour = var)
qplot(block, value, data = subset(rm, type == "theta"), colour = var)

# Vertical shading - just draw a line in the background

ggplot(subset(rm, type == "cov"), aes(block, value)) +
geom_vline(aes(xintercept = block), subset = .(Inversion == "yes"),
size = 5, colour = "grey70") +
geom_point(aes(colour = var))

# Or with colours
# This requires a little trickier if we want different scales for the
# background lines and points. Fortunately, we can use filled points
# and the fill aesthetic
ggplot(subset(rm, type == "cov"), aes(block, value)) +
geom_vline(aes(xintercept = block, colour = Inversion),
size = 5, alpha = 0.2) +
geom_point(aes(fill = var), shape = 21, colour = NA)

Hadley

--
http://had.co.nz/

As an update for others struggling with vertical lines, I still have
not sorted out how to do shading in between different vertical lines,
but thanks to another post in the google group, I saw that having aes
in the geom_vline function seems to NOT work. I still don't have
insight as to why this is and would like to gain that insight if
anyone else has it.

Anyway, I have a plot that goes from 0 to 100,000,000 on the X axis
and I plotted vertical lines at the places I need them by
geom_vline(xintercept=c
(18930000,26764357,31450000,82024058,103665182))

rather than by using Inversion (see earlier post above) as a
categorical variable (yes vs no). I'm still curious how to make
several different color backgrounds in between a few of the vertical
lines I've drawn so it would be easier to distinguish which
"Inversion" is which. Between 18930000 and 26764357 is inversion 1,
between 26764357 and 31450000 is inversion 2, and between 82024058 and
103665182 is inversion 3. These values won't change and so I just need
to plot them as an addition on each figure rather than needing
something that can read an actual variable, so if anyone has any great
ideas, thanks.

Best,
Mara.
